I'll start by exploring the workspace to understand the project structure and find `main.go`.The baseline builds and tests pass. Here's my proposal before implementing:

**Proposal:** Keep everything in `main.go` but introduce a minimal dependency-injection structure:
- `Adder` - a one-method interface (the narrow contract the app needs)
- `Calculator` - a struct whose `Add` method owns the real helper
- `Service` - holds an injected `Adder`, so application logic can be tested with a fake instead of real arithmetic

`add` stays as the single arithmetic implementation so the existing test remains untouched and green. Then I will add a test that injects a fake `Adder` to prove the structure actually improves testability.Now let me verify the module builds and all tests pass, including `go vet` and formatting checks.Done. All checks are green:

- `gofmt -l .` no output (formatting clean)
- `go vet ./...` clean
- `go build ./...` passes
- `go test ./... -v` passes, including the original `TestAdd`

## Architecture change

I kept the change contained in `main.go` and made it minimal:

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| `Adder` interface | One-method contract. Tests can substitute a tiny fake instead of real arithmetic. |
| `Calculator` struct | Owns the real helper as an `Add` method, so it satisfies `Adder`. |
| `Service` struct + `NewService` | Application-facing code depends on `Adder`, not on the concrete helper. This is the part that becomes easy to test. |
| `add` function | Stays as the single source of arithmetic, so the existing test compiles and passes unchanged. |

`main()` is unchanged, so runtime behavior is untouched.

## Why this makes the helper easy to test

Before, the only way to exercise the helper was a direct call to the package function. Now the app logic sits behind an injected interface, so `service_test.go` can pass a `fakeAdder` that records calls and returns a fixed value. That test asserts both the returned result and the interaction, which would be impossible with a hard-coded direct call.

I also added a table-driven test for `Calculator.Add` covering positive, negative and zero inputs, plus a test confirming `NewService` works with the real `Calculator`.

Files changed: `main.go` (modified) and `service_test.go` (new). `main_test.go` and `go.mod` were left untouched.
